option_relations.rationale: Lichen planus pigmentosus is a variant of lichen planus characterized by hyperpigmented macules and patches, often in sun-exposed areas, and is distinct from discoid eczema.
Inverse lichen planus is a variant of lichen planus affecting intertriginous areas, but it is a distinct condition from discoid eczema.
Lichenoid drug eruption is a reaction to medication that mimics lichen planus, but it is not discoid eczema.
Discoid lupus erythematosus is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease primarily affecting the skin, characterized by discoid lesions, but it is distinct from discoid eczema.
